Security & Compliance.description: GIO service line for the Group's security solutions, from identity and access to cloud and application protection, vulnerability management and incident response.
Security & Compliance.scope: Designs, builds and runs the Group's security solutions: identity and access, network security and remote access, cloud security, application protection, hardening and compliance, PKI and certificates, vulnerability management, security architecture and CSIRT.
notThis: Site firewalls, WAN rules and site edge belong to Site Infrastructure — this line owns corporate vulnerability management, security architecture and CSIRT, not the site perimeter.
Rolling a new access client out to end users is User Workplace as a consumer; the ZPA/ZTNA platform itself is owned here.

Command Center.description: GIO service line acting as the transversal hub that monitors and coordinates digital operations around the clock.
Command Center.scope: Transversal hub monitoring and coordinating digital operations 24/7: major incident management, observability and monitoring, service orchestration (SIAM), data quality and CMDB, AIOps and automation.
notThis: Building the monitored service is the owning service line's work; this line owns watching and coordinating it.

User Workplace.description: GIO service line owning the employee digital environment: devices, collaboration tools, corporate app distribution and end-user support.
User Workplace.scope: The employee digital environment: PCs, mobile devices, videoconferencing, Google Workspace, corporate app stores, local and remote support. Initiatives include cloud device management, managed printing, self-service portal and ServiceNow automation.
notThis: The remote-access platform (ZPA/VPN) is owned by Security & Compliance; this line appears only as the consumer of a rollout to users.

Site Infrastructure.description: GIO service line owning the local digital foundations of the Group's sites: networks, site security equipment and local compute.
Site Infrastructure.scope: Physical and local digital foundations of roughly 3,000 sites: LAN, WAN, Wi-Fi, Cisco ISE, site firewalls (WAN rules and site edge) and local compute.
notThis: Corporate vulnerability management, security architecture and CSIRT belong to Security & Compliance.
Cloud connectivity belongs to Cloud Services.
Site Infrastructure.notes: Renamed from GIO Network & Telecom; both names still appear in documents because of the transition.

Cloud Services.description: GIO service line owning the Group's multi-cloud strategy and environment, including the deployment framework, cost management and service-account policy.
Cloud Services.scope: Multi-cloud strategy and environment (AWS, GCP): a standardised, automated and secure deployment framework, FinOps, and security policies for service accounts.
notThis: Wi-Fi is Site Infrastructure. "Wi-Fi on the Cloud" is a roadmap item, not ownership.
Cloud security POLICY is set with Security & Compliance; this line owns the environment.

Americas.description: Regional hub overseeing North America (NAM), Argentina (ARG), and Latin America (LATAM). Includes major subsidiaries such as Airgas.
Americas.scope: Regional hub covering North America (NAM), Argentina (ARG) and Latin America (LATAM).
notThis: Airgas is a separate entity whose parent is Americas — mark Airgas when the text is about Airgas.

Europe.description: Regional hub managing a perimeter that includes Central Europe (CE), South West Europe (SWE), and North East Europe (NEC).
Europe.scope: Regional hub organised in the business clusters CE (Central Europe), SWE (South-West Europe) and NEC (North-East Europe), which govern billing, customer portfolio and IT portfolio.
notThis: EAMEI is a GIO regional direction, not a DDS entity. A document saying EAMEI marks Europe only when the scope is the whole region; otherwise mark whatever the text identifies by country or site.
GIO delivery clusters do not define DDS Europe.

APAC.description: Regional hub covering Greater China (GCH) and the broader Asia-Pacific region.
APAC.scope: Regional hub covering Greater China (GCH) and the rest of Asia-Pacific.

AMEI.description: Regional hub responsible for digital operations across Africa, Middle East, and India.
AMEI.scope: Regional hub covering Africa, the Middle East and India.
notThis: EAMEI alone does not mark AMEI — see Europe.

CF.description: Corporate Functions. Covers critical Group domains including Finance, HR, Procurement, Communication, Legal, and Intellectual Property.
CF.scope: Corporate Functions: Finance, HR, Procurement, Communication, Legal and Intellectual Property.

GM&T.description: Global Markets & Technologies. A business division supported by dedicated D&IT Business Partners.
GM&T.notes: The IDD IT groups that sat under GM&T moved to InnoTech; the BIS GM&T provider is still live, so GM&T stays canonical. The BGMT trigram is not an alias until that provider is retired.

HC D&IT.description: Healthcare Digital & Information Technology. Provides specialised digital services for the Healthcare business line.
HC D&IT.scope: Healthcare Digital & Information Technology: the technology-governance function of the Healthcare vertical — IT leadership, architecture validation, and compliance with global security and IT-procurement standards.
notThis: Business operations, users and care programmes belong to HHC.

Alizent.description: Subsidiary focused on industrial IoT and asset tracking.
Alizent.scope: Subsidiary for industrial IoT and asset tracking.

GDO.description: Global Digital Organization. The central driver for digital transformation and innovation across the Group.
GDO.scope: Global Data Operations: the data operations entity inside Global Delivery Services.
notThis: The GDO acronym appears in documents of 64 of 69 analysed projects. Being mentioned is not being impacted — claim it only when the project changes or depends on GDO's work.

SEPPIC.description: Specialty healthcare and beauty ingredient subsidiary, maintained as its own DDS entity.
SEPPIC.scope: Subsidiary producing specialty ingredients for health and beauty, kept as a DDS entity of its own.

Airgas.description: Key entity within the Americas hub, specifically focused on industrial and medical gas markets.
Airgas.scope: Industrial and medical gas markets in the United States, integrated into the Americas organisational structure.
notThis: Do not also claim Americas for the same evidence — the aggregation is done downstream, not by adding a second claim.

HHC.description: Home Healthcare. Manages digital solutions for chronic patient care, such as the kairin respiratory monitoring solution.
HHC.scope: The Home Healthcare vertical on both the business and the delivery side: the global GBU (operations, operational excellence, care programmes) and the DDS HHC IT service provider.
notThis: HC D&IT is the technology-governance function for the same vertical. Business process, users, operations or a care programme → HHC. IT delivery, architecture, tooling or technical compliance → HC D&IT.
Provider support ("DDS HHC: support") is HHC, not HC D&IT.

Industrial Apps.description: Group within GDS that partners with Industrial Direction to define technical product roadmaps.
Industrial Apps.scope: Works with the Industrial Direction to define product technical roadmaps.

Enterprise Apps.description: Group focused on digital solutions for core enterprise-wide business processes.
Enterprise Apps.scope: Digital solutions for the corporate processes that cut across the Group.

Data & AI Apps.description: Specialised technical chapter within GDS dedicated to managing data strategy and artificial intelligence products.

Digital Factory.description: Delivery engine within GDS responsible for the rapid development and scaling of digital products.
Digital Factory.scope: Delivery engine: agile development and scaling of digital products.

InnoTech.description: GBU formed by merging the IDD and E&C divisions. Both former names still appear in older documents and resolve here.
InnoTech.scope: GBU created by merging IDD (Innovation & Development) and E&C (Engineering & Construction).
InnoTech.notes: E&C and IDD are no longer targets of their own; older documents still use both names. The DIN and BEC trigrams normalise structured fields only, never free text.

CDIO Office.description: Office of the Chief Digital & Information Officer. Sets the Group's overall Digital & IT vision and governance.
CDIO Office.scope: Office of the Chief Digital & Information Officer: sets the Group's Digital & IT vision and governance.
